Validation

Source: VALIDATION.md

Current implementation

The fork is based on upstream R master ecd384343c53903517aa903ed7c8a150f4c5dc93, with the mixed-input ordering correction in lgp() ported from upstream dev a62a319af8eeeafce541acade0887601b117e6f8. The clean master branch remains unchanged. The DGP training constructor and prunlgp search and objective are unchanged.

The recorded environment is Windows 11, R 4.4.2, Python 3.10.20 and Python dgpsi source 480bb30260d3a1c22af1ddffe1a11df3e4de0820. R sessions and package libraries are separate; existing dependencies and the Python runtime are reused.

Why input ordering matters

When a receiving DGP uses both global and internal inputs, the linked backend consumes internal inputs first. The earlier master constructor remapped the connection indices without consistently reordering the deep-layer training inputs and their lengthscales. The correction aligns these quantities and orders connection-table rows by their receiving input positions.

An independent regression check uses an upstream GP whose maximum prediction error is 0.00000293. Passing its prediction through a link should closely agree with passing the corresponding observed value. The maximum downstream mean difference was 1.784694 with the previous mapping and 0.00000773 after correction. The regression also checks predictive variances and invariance to connection-row order. It tests actual information transmission, rather than inferring correct linking from different RMSE values.

The earlier apparent pruning benefits were affected by this input-order error. The historical record preserves the published numbers through f62b778. The results below supersede those numbers.

Unchanged data and selection settings

Both tutorials keep their data, seed and fitting budget. Each scalar DGP uses two layers, two latent nodes, the squared exponential kernel, 40 iterations, 10 ESS burn-in steps per iteration and 20 imputations. Seed 57 controls matched original/refitted component seeds and stable component imputation streams.

Pruning minimises mean validation NRMSE. The normalising scales come from training responses. With protect=0, an admissible candidate cannot worsen any scored validation output beyond numerical tolerance. The search uses two subset passes and at most 32 evaluations. Neither the retained sources nor the number of retained connections is prescribed. The test set does not select the graph.

Operational example

The same prunlgp_example.csv supplies 96 training, 48 validation and 96 test rows, two intermediate responses and three scored responses. Causal filtering, training-only scaling and the prediction information set are unchanged. The CSV is byte-identical to the earlier release, SHA-256:

cc22f368c4d863a75efdf91c2b7ff29df24fcfb8b63205ffc971633f75b9bd07.

The corrected run retains u to a and v to c, removing the other four internal connections independently. Both intermediate models therefore supply a retained downstream prediction. Model b continues to predict from its global inputs; no output model is deleted.

Quantity Unpruned Pruned
Internal connections 6 2
Validation mean NRMSE 0.470206 0.459021
Test mean NRMSE 0.444737 0.475874
Output Validation unpruned Validation pruned Test unpruned Test pruned
a 0.762719 0.761562 0.789238 0.854998
b 0.435682 0.405167 0.302891 0.324359
c 0.212217 0.210332 0.242083 0.248266

The search record also shows why u was retained. Starting from the selected input subsets, the evaluated candidate that removes u from a and refits that receiver increases a’s validation RMSE from 0.761562 to 0.871652. The other two outputs’ errors remain unchanged. That candidate is rejected by validation protection. This is an observed predictive contribution of u, not a rule requiring the algorithm to retain at least one outgoing link from each source.

All three validation errors decrease, but all three test errors increase. This operational example demonstrates output-specific selection and the limits of validation protection; it does not establish a held-out accuracy advantage. The CSV was not replaced or screened to force a preferred retained graph. It is a retrospective tutorial sample used in earlier development, not a new prospective field evaluation.

Synthetic example

The unchanged generator provides 80 training, 120 validation and 240 independent test rows. The corrected network retains u to a, u to b, and v to c.

Quantity Unpruned Pruned
Internal connections 6 3
Validation mean NRMSE 0.191363 0.180517
Test mean NRMSE 0.178999 0.169024

All three validation and test errors decrease. The generating equation for b uses only global inputs, yet retaining u improves finite-sample prediction. Predictive input selection does not identify causal relationships. These numbers reproduce the earlier dev-based comparison with the corresponding input-order correction ported to master.

Reproduction

Both tutorial runners refit their models and save the actual candidate records, structures and per-output errors. The published articles come from executed R Markdown. The package checks and native tests are separate from tutorial fits. The input-order regression extends the native suite to 13 cases and 52 expectations, all passed with no failures, warnings or skips on 12 November 2026. R CMD build --no-manual and R CMD check --no-manual --no-build-vignettes completed with Status: OK. The earlier tests also cover grouped copies, independent receivers, unchanged paths, zero links, serialization and parallel candidate evaluation.

Follow PRUNLGP.md for installation, Python setup, test commands, tutorial execution and upstream synchronization. Cross-platform numerical identity is not established by the Windows verification.
